paper_topic: LASCon: Loop-Aware Scratchpad Condensation, a training-free scaffold combining deterministic CLI condensation and progress-conditioned loop control for terminal agents
anchor_paper: Wang et al., 2025 (OpenHands / LLM-based summarization baseline)

nodes.text: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed for command-line interface (CLI) tasks, from software engineering to system administration (Yang et al., 2024a; Jimenez et al., 2023).
nodes.display_label: LLM agents deployed for CLI tasks

nodes.text: These agents interact with terminal environments through iterative reasoning and action cycles (Yao et al., 2022), executing commands and processing outputs to accomplish complex goals.

Recent benchmarks such as Terminal-Bench (Merrill et al., 2026) evaluate agents on realistic CLI tasks requiring multi-step reasoning, revealing that long-horizon interactions pose significant challenges: as trajectories grow, context windows fill with observation histories, leading to timeout failures and degraded performance.
Existing agent frameworks address context growth through LLM-based summarization, compressing older observations into free-form summaries (Wang et al., 2025).
However, CLI environments present unique challenges for such approaches.
Terminal outputs contain exact tokens critical for task completion—specific error messages, file paths, and command flags—that free-form summaries may omit or paraphrase incorrectly.
nodes.display_label: free-form summaries lose exact CLI tokens

nodes.text: Additionally, agents may enter unproductive loops, repeatedly executing the same failing command without making progress.
Current stuck detectors typically terminate execution upon detecting such patterns, preventing resource waste
but not helping the agent recover.
We present LASCon (Loop-Aware Scratchpad Condensation), a training-free scaffold intervention that addresses these challenges through two complementary modules.

The Deterministic CLI Condenser (DCC) replaces LLM-based summarization with rule-based extraction tailored to CLI outputs, preserving commands, exit codes, error lines, and truncated outputs while offloading full logs to disk.
nodes.display_label: DCC: rule-based CLI extraction, logs to disk

nodes.text: The Progress-Conditioned Loop Controller (PLC) converts loop detection into action-space shaping, blocking specific repeated actions to force exploration of alternatives rather than terminating execution.
On Terminal-Bench 2.0 with Qwen3-32B, LASCon achieves 68.8% completion rate (+21.2pp over baseline) while eliminating all timeout failures.
LASCon: A training-free scaffold combining deterministic CLI condensation with progress-conditioned loop control, deployable with any LLM backend without fine-tuning.
Empirical finding: Structured context management through DCC alone achieves 70.0% completion (+18.8pp), demonstrating that deterministic condensation outperforms LLM summarization for CLI contexts.
Analysis: Loop-induced failures are rare (2.5% in baseline) and eliminated by prompting alone; PLC serves as a conservative safety net (0.12% block rate) rather than a primary improvement mechanism.
nodes.display_label: PLC is safety net, not primary driver

Fork/join structure: N9 (LASCon overview) forks into the two method components N10 (DCC) and N11 (PLC). These two components join into N12 (the headline result), which then forks into the three contribution items. The Limitation chain N5 -> N6 -> N7 -> N8pw -> N8 contains a parallel pair (summarization-loss, loop-failure) but is presented sequentially in prose. N8pw is a Prior_Work split out of the original N8 sentence so the stuck-detector method description has its own PW node, while N8 carries only the 'but not helping recover' critique clause.

Anchor paper: Wang et al. 2025 (OpenHands), the LLM-summarization baseline that LASCon explicitly replaces and integrates with.

Notable features: Two clean addresses edges with strong lexical overlap. N10 (DCC: rule-based extraction preserving 'commands, exit codes, error lines') addresses N6 (free-form summaries omit 'specific error messages, file paths, and command flags'). N11 (PLC: blocking actions 'rather than terminating execution') addresses N8 (stuck detectors 'terminate execution ... but not helping the agent recover'). The third contribution N15 honestly down-weights the PLC component, which is unusual self-criticism for an AI-generated paper.
